slides.title: Real data is messy
slides.text: People make typos, answer twice or write numbers that can not be true. Chart messy data and the chart tells the wrong story.
slides.alt: The Twelve Pets case as it arrived: a messy table where one kind of pet hides under several spellings.

slides.title: Clean it first
slides.text: Fix typos, merge true repeats and remove values that can not be true. Never remove a row just because you do not like its answer.
slides.alt: Double Trouble: a second messy case, where the same student answered twice and one row must go.

slides.title: Pet survey clean-up
slides.text: Three spellings of dog split one bar into three short bars. Clean first, then chart.
slides.alt: The cleaned pet chart: the three misspelled dogs are fixed to one spelling, and the Dog bar counts all seven.

slides.title: Compare by percent
slides.text: Class A: 9 of 20 like chess. Class B: 12 of 40. B has more, but A is 45% and B is 30%. Percent is part divided by whole, times 100.
slides.alt: Tidy, Then Compare: two cleaned sets side by side, the case where comparing fairly means comparing percents.

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Data Detective at Clean-Up Crew and solve 4 cases. Chart the data as it is first, then clean it and chart it again. What changed?
